# SHARED SEMANTIC-ENVELOPE TRANSCRIPT INVENTORY (task 1.5-i).
#
# FIVE PRINCIPAL INVENTORIES PLUS SEPARATELY GUARDED EXCLUSION AND RELATION SETS -- SEVEN KEYED
# SETS IN ALL, EACH GUARDED ON ITS OWN, AND NO GRAND TOTAL. They count
# different proof units, so adding them would invent a number that means nothing: a root slot is
# a CLOSURE VIEW, a framer operation is a LEXICAL WRITE inside one framer, a state case is an
# ALTERNATIVE branch, an attachment edge is a COMPOSITION-GRAPH edge, and a separation row is a
# quantity that must NOT reach the transcript. Each section is checked for its exact key set AND
# its count, on its own terms.
#
# `op` -- FRAMER-LOCAL OPERATIONS (125). Deliberately NOT "every primitive callsite": that would
# be 138, since the root slots contribute 13 direct writes on top of these. Nested members are
# keyed under the sub-message that owns them (`delivery_claims.transition.*`,
# `execution_grant_claims.source_identity.*`), so a key names a path and not just a leaf.
#
# `slot` -- ROOT SLOTS (17): the version prefix plus record fields 1..16, TWELVE direct and
# FOUR composite. The direct/composite column is DERIVED FROM THE DESCRIPTOR by both consumers,
# not copied from here, so relabelling a slot fails rather than passing unread. A closure view,
# NOT seventeen further writes. THE ORDER OF THESE SLOTS IS NOT A SLOT ROW: per-slot inequality
# is blind to it -- swapping two composite blocks leaves every slot row green -- so it is carried
# by an ORDERED SEVENTEEN-CHUNK DECOMPOSITION of the root transcript, one chunk per direct write
# and one per composite child's framed output, which is CONCATENATED AND HASHED BACK TO THE
# PRODUCTION DIGEST before anything is concluded from it. Unbound, it was a second test-only
# grammar free to drift -- and it had, silently omitting `producer_context` entirely. No two
# chunks may concatenate identically IN EITHER ORDER; plain inequality is not enough for
# variable-length chunks, since A||B can equal B||A for distinct A and B. The whole-envelope
# base shape's vectors `root.shape.base.v0..v2` NAME that measurement; `v0` shares its value with
# FIVE `state.*.present` rows -- producer_context, capability, capability@source_auth,
# source_authorization and output_contract@root -- which measure the same thing, so SIX keys move
# together. That set is ASSERTED, not just written here: `TestSemanticBaseShapeAliasSetIsExact`
# and its Elixir peer rebuild it from these vectors and fail on drift. The `version` slot is REUSED
# EVIDENCE from `version_corpus.txt`: only Go can parameterise the grammar version, and this
# runtime's `SemanticDigest.compute/1` takes no version argument, so no row here re-proves it.
#
# `state` -- ALTERNATIVES. FIVE PRESENCE RULES across SIX CARRIER PAIRS (the capability rule
# has TWO carriers: the record's production slot and source_auth's nested one) (one row each, NOT an increment to the operation
# count), the two discriminant sets with EXACT values, and the single optU64 site. Presence and
# discriminant rows SHALL pin EXACT framed bytes or a committed digest: absent and present
# already differ in most fixtures for unrelated reasons, so INEQUALITY ALONE would survive
# deleting the marker. `authority_epoch` is the ONLY optU64; the AuthorityEpoch fields in
# production/source/execution-grant claims are plain u64 and are cited here so no reader infers
# five optional sites.
#
# The delivery transition is pinned in FIVE states, not two: `unset`, and each of `renewal` and
# `rollover` both DEFAULTED and POPULATED. The defaulted pair pins the discriminant; the populated
# pair pins the order and width INSIDE the branch.
# A defaulted renewal writes two zero i64s and a defaulted rollover two empty byte strings, so
# swapping either pair is a NO-OP there -- measured: both swaps were invisible until the
# populated bodies were committed.
#
# `edge` -- COMPOSITION GRAPH (13), NOT thirteen independent proofs. Edges OVERLAP operation and
# slot evidence: deleting one call can fail rows in several sections at once. Each row targets
# the deletion of THAT call OR INLINE BLOCK, and overlapping failures are recorded honestly rather than counted
# as separate coverage. ALL THIRTEEN ARE DERIVED FROM THE DESCRIPTORS and compared in BOTH
# DIRECTIONS: the nested walk finds four, the record's composite slots four more, and the claims
# oneof the last five -- whose {field number, child root} pairs are pinned, since those numbers
# ARE the transcript's discriminant values and renumbering two members relabels every framed
# claim while the member set, the count and the child framers all stay identical. Deriving only
# four left nine declared-and-underived, where deleting a declaration was indistinguishable from
# deleting a carrier.
#
# `sep` -- SEPARATION. Quantities that must NOT influence the semantic digest -- spool
# coordinates, `delivery_capability`, the physical artifact identity, and the producer-receipt
# identity. These are frame FIELDS; 1.5-j owns broker PUBLICATION IDENTITY, a different object, one mutated per
# row. FOUR of the five vary a LIVE quantity in both runtimes; `producer_receipt.submission_sha256`
# is different in kind -- it is SCHEMA CLOSURE over a field that does not exist anywhere in the
# edge protos, so there is nothing to vary and nothing to mutate. Do not read the five as a
# uniform set.
#
# VALUE DISTINCTNESS IS SCOPED TO THE WHOLE FLAT TRANSCRIPT, because there is no smaller scope.
# The preimage is an UNTAGGED CONCATENATION: no length prefix, no intermediate hash, no framing
# around a child block. A helper in either implementation is therefore INVISIBLE to it -- calling
# `producerContext` instead of writing its fields inline changes no byte and separates nothing --
# so every write coexists with every other, and two writes of the same wire class carrying the
# same value are exchangeable without moving a byte. THE WIRE CLASS IS THE WIDTH: `i64` is
# `u64(uint64(v))` and `str` is `bytes([]byte(s))`, so those pairs are indistinguishable and are
# guarded as one class.
#
# NEITHER RUNTIME'S HELPER STRUCTURE IS EVIDENCE OF ANYTHING, and the CARRIER'S OWN DECISIONS
# need their own rows. A seam vector freezes what a framer does when TOLD a carrier is absent; it
# says nothing about the root inferring `c != nil`, and replacing that inference with a literal
# `true` was invisible until a whole-record ABSENT witness existed for each of the four carriers.
# Likewise the claim bodies and the discriminant have vectors, but neither sees the capability
# transcript AROUND them, so reordering the claims against the signature FOR ONE VARIANT the
# record never carried was invisible until every composed capability shape was framed at the root.
#
# ONE FIXTURE CANNOT SEPARATE THE ROOT, and that is arithmetic. Its transcript carries thirteen
# enum writes -- SEVEN with a range of 0..2 -- plus the structural constants. Seven positions
# cannot take seven distinct values from three. So a position's identity is its SIGNATURE, the
# tuple of values it takes across a shape's VARIANTS, and THREE are needed: no position may take
# an all-equal tuple (one that never varies could equal a structural constant, and a shape whose
# only content is root enums would frame identically in every variant -- measured), and a range
# of 3 yields only SIX varying tuples over two variants against SEVEN positions. Three yield
# twenty-four. The claim baselines are committed PER VARIANT for the same reason: the cross
# product puts two claim bodies in one transcript, and constant-valued sets cannot separate them.
#
# TWO POSITIONS COLLIDE ONLY IF THEY AGREE IN EVERY VARIANT OF THE SHAPE THEY BOTH OCCUR IN.
# Asking it across the whole fixture set is too weak -- a mutation executes inside ONE shape, and
# `compression` and a claims discriminant were both 0 in the shape where production claims are
# unset and the nested carrier holds `source`. TWO STRUCTURAL CONSTANTS ARE EXEMPT: two carriers
# holding the same claims kind write the same discriminant by force of the shape, so no fixture of
# it can separate them and no swap confined there changes anything for ANY input. A pair with a
# FIELD on either side is never exempt: its equality is the fixture's choice, not the shape's.
#
# THREE SCOPES WERE WRONG BEFORE THIS ONE, each leaving a live survivor: per MESSAGE let
# `execution_grant_claims.traffic_class` and its inlined `source_identity.kind` both take 0; per
# HELPER let the root's `traffic_class` and `producer_context.origin_kind` both take 0; and
# guarding only the BASE SHAPE let `payload_family` and `compression` -- both zero in the first
# variant -- be swapped whenever the capability carried `collection`.
#
# EVERY WHOLE-RECORD SHAPE IS A FIXTURE. Reconstructing a shape byte for byte shows the mirror
# agrees with production for it; it says nothing about whether two writes INSIDE it are
# exchangeable, so every shape is built at every variant, signature-guarded and committed.
#
# AND NO HAND-PICKED MATRIX EVER CONVERGES. Five review rounds each found a reordering
# conditioned on some state no fixture held -- a claims variant, a carrier, a PAIR of carriers,
# then a pair the fixtures held but the guard compared globally -- and each round added the
# missing case. The space of predicates a framer COULD branch on is unbounded, so no finite
# fixture set is complete against it.
#
# SO THE MATRIX IS ENUMERATED FROM THE DECLARED AXES rather than chosen, and it is exhaustive
# OVER THOSE AXES:
#
#   output_contract presence   2
#   producer_context presence  2, and its optional authority_epoch when present -> 3
#   production capability     10 states
#   source_authorization      11: absent, or present with its capability in 10 states
#
# 2 x 3 x 10 x 11 = 660 shapes, plus the base record, at three variants each. The enumeration says
# every combination of what the grammar DECLARES it branches on is committed. The static guards
# are a separate, weaker thing: they check that the framers keep that shape, and they do not
# establish that nothing else can branch -- see their limits below.
#
# EXHAUSTIVE OVER THE DECLARED AXES, NOT OVER EVERY PROGRAM THE HOST LANGUAGES CAN EXPRESS. The
# cross product covers every combination of carrier presence and oneof discriminant the grammar
# declares. It does NOT cover a framer that branches on something else -- and the static guards
# that CHECK FOR RECOGNIZED FORMS of that are DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH REGRESSION CHECKS, not a proof. Their known limits, stated
# so no reader infers more: the Go guard identifies proto and oneof accessors BY NAME, so a method
# spelled `GetClaims` on an unrelated type is accepted; the Elixir guard reads function BODIES and
# does not resolve function heads, guards, macro expansions or remote calls, so a two-clause helper
# matching `%{projected_row_count: 42}` is invisible to it. Closing that needs a descriptor-validated
# declarative grammar that GENERATES both framers, recorded as an UNOWNED follow-up -- not a second pair
# of analyzers chasing two host languages from the outside.
#
# SEPARATION IS ASKED PER SHAPE, NOT ACROSS THE WHOLE FIXTURE SET. A mutation executes inside ONE
# shape, so a pair must be separated by a variant OF THAT SHAPE -- asked globally, `compression`
# and a claims discriminant were both 0 in the shape where production claims are unset and the
# nested carrier holds `source`, and swapping them there moved no byte. Two STRUCTURAL CONSTANTS
# are exempt: when both carriers hold the same claims kind their discriminants are forced equal by
# the shape itself, and a swap confined to such a shape changes nothing for ANY input. A pair with
# a FIELD on either side is never exempt -- its equality is the fixture's choice.
#
# THE CLAIM BASELINES SHARE THE RECORD'S GENERATION PASS, IN TWO SETS, PER VARIANT. A baseline is
# spliced into a shape, so its writes land in the record's transcript; generated independently, a
# record position and a claim position held the same value. The cross product then puts TWO claim
# bodies in one transcript, so one set is not enough either, and disjoint VALUES cannot separate
# them -- `production_claims` alone needs three distinct values from fields of range 3, 4 and 3,
# which exhausts the range-3 space for a single carrier. The separation is by SIGNATURE across
# variants. Measured on the way here: one shared set gave 202 collisions, two constant-valued
# sets still gave 39.
#
# THE PRIMITIVE INVENTORY IS AN ORDERED MIRROR, BOUND BYTE FOR BYTE. Every conclusion above rests
# on "these are exactly the writes, in exactly this order". A width SUM cannot establish that: it
# is blind to an equal-width omission paired with an equal-width addition, and to any
# substitution at all. So the mirror emits each primitive's exact bytes in transcript order and
# its concatenation must EQUAL the preimage the seventeen chunks reconstruct -- itself proven
# equal to production by hashing. It is checked for every committed variant, for each
# carrier-absent shape and for each composed capability shape, so a branch the mirror gets wrong
# cannot hide in an unexercised shape.
#
# PRESENCE MARKERS AND ZERO-LENGTH WRITES CARRY NO VALUE and are excluded from the signature
# guard by name: a 1-byte marker and a bare length prefix cannot be made distinct, and exchanging
# two identical writes is not observable in principle. Presence is discharged by the `state` rows
# instead, which vary it.
#
# `sep` closure walks EVERY message in the package INCLUDING NESTED TYPES, carries
# an ACCEPTED CONTROL (a field that IS present must be found by the same walk, or "found
# nothing" would equally describe a scan that reached nothing), and asserts a nonzero scanned
# inventory. The edge package declares no nested messages and no map fields today, so the
# recursive branch is exercised against a descriptor built for the purpose rather than left to
# be assumed correct.
#
# PROBE:
#   preimage  exact framed bytes at a framing seam -- PUBLIC in Elixir (`ClaimsFraming`),
#             same-package PRIVATE in Go, so "seam" means reachable-by-the-suite, not exported.
#             THE TWO RUNTIMES REACH THE CLAIM BODIES AT DIFFERENT DEPTHS: Go calls each claim
#             framer directly, while Elixir has only `claims_framed/1`, which prefixes the
#             discriminant -- so its adapter slices those 8 bytes off to compare bodies. The
#             prefix is therefore NOT covered by those rows on the Elixir side; the
#             `state.claims_discriminant.*` vectors cover it separately, so the gap is closed by
#             a different row rather than left open.
#   digest    one-field mutation through the public digest entry point
#   attach    deletion of the call must change the digest
#   closure   descriptor-driven, both directions
#   exclude   the quantity must NOT change the recomputed digest
#   relation  the quantity reaches the transcript only THROUGH another committed value
#   invariant the quantity must leave the digest unchanged while it varies
#   committed the assertion is against a COMMITTED digest vector, not an ad-hoc recomputation
#             and not an inequality: deleting a presence marker leaves absent/present unequal
#             anyway, so only a frozen expected value discriminates it
#   reuse     the obligation is discharged by a NAMED row in another corpus; no row here
#             re-proves it, and the detail column names that row
#
# ADMISSION-INVALID RECORDS ARE INTENTIONAL. Rows mutate ONE occurrence and SHALL NOT
# synchronise a duplicate field, reseal a capability, or validate the record: a second changed
# occurrence can mask a deleted write, which is the defect these rows exist to find.
#
# kind  key                                                                detail       probe

excl  17.semantic_envelope_sha256                                         self         exclude

rel   18.payload->06.payload_sha256                                      transitive   relation
#       CONSTRUCTION, normative for this row: the two payloads are EQUAL LENGTH and the size
#       fields are HELD FIXED, so the only normalized difference is the payload bytes and, in
#       the second half, `payload_sha256`. Unequal lengths would move encoded_size/
#       uncompressed_size too and the row would prove those slots instead.
sep   producer_receipt.submission_sha256                                 schema-absent closure
sep   physical_artifact.record_sha256.legal_reencoding                   reencode     invariant
sep   delivery_frame.spool_id                                            outer-frame  invariant
sep   delivery_frame.sequence                                            outer-frame  invariant
sep   delivery_frame.delivery_capability                                 outer-frame  invariant
